data: Before we choose, can we agree on a shared catch limit? I propose 18 tons each this month: 90 total, leaving 10. Next month we’d have either 100 tons or 20 tons—not a guaranteed refill. For future months, each person’s quota could be one-fifth of the stock above a protected 10-ton reserve, rounded down to whole tons. At 20 tons, that means 2 tons each. We can review everyone’s revealed catches and adjust together each month. I’m willing to follow this plan if everyone agrees. John, would you support it?

I support a shared limit, Emma. Could we protect 5 tons instead of 10? That lets us take 19 tons each now while still qualifying for the 75% refill chance. If it fails, we’d start next month with 10 tons and take just 1 ton each, leaving 5 again. For future months, everyone’s quota would be the stock above 5 divided by five, rounded down. This preserves the fishery even through repeated failed refills, provided everyone respects the cap. I’ll follow whichever reserve we all agree on. John, what do you think?

I support Luke’s 5-ton reserve: 19 tons each now, then a whole-ton quota of the current stock minus 5, divided by five and rounded down. The refill chance is the same with either reserve, and this rule keeps at least 5 tons even if refills repeatedly fail—as long as everyone sticks to it. Let’s make the quota a firm ceiling, not a target anyone can exceed, and review the revealed catches together each month. I’ll commit if all five of us agree. Kate, Jack, are you on board—and Emma, would you accept the smaller reserve?

I’m on board with the 5-ton reserve and will cap my catch at 19 tons this month if all five agree. In later months, I’ll follow the whole-ton quota John described, based on the actual stock—not an assumed refill. Since one person exceeding the cap could jeopardize everyone’s future income, let’s explicitly confirm our commitments before choosing. Kate, are you in? Emma, would you accept this revision?

I’m in: I’ll catch no more than 19 tons this month if all five agree, and follow the stock-based whole-ton quota thereafter. The 5-ton reserve leaves no room for an overrun, so if anyone wants to revise the cap, let’s discuss it before choosing—not exceed it privately. Emma, does this revision work for you?
